retention.title: Data Retention
retention.description: Configure how long audit logs and activity events are kept. Backup retention is configured on each container backup schedule. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.auditDaysDescription: Number of days to keep audit log entries. Older entries are automatically purged.
retention.activityDaysDescription: Number of days to keep container activity events. Older events are automatically purged.
retention.backupDaysDescription: Maximum number of days to keep successful backups per container. Older backup archives are deleted automatically. Set to 0 to keep backups regardless of age.
retention.backupCountDescription: Maximum number of successful backups to keep per container. Older backup archives are deleted automatically. Set to 0 to keep all backups.
retention.clearNowHint: Run the retention purge now (entries older than {{days}} days)
retention.clearAuditDescription: Permanently delete all audit log entries older than {{days}} days. The deleted count will be shown after the operation. This cannot be undone.
retention.clearActivityDescription: Permanently delete all activity events older than {{days}} days. The deleted count will be shown after the operation. This cannot be undone.
retention.keepForever: Set retention to a positive number to enable clearing.
retention.lifecycleDaysDescription: Days to keep lifecycle events before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.backupLogDaysDescription: Days to keep backup-log rows before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.scanDaysDescription: Days to keep vulnerability scans (and their findings) before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.clearLifecycleDescription: Permanently delete every lifecycle event older than {{days}} days. This action cannot be undone.
retention.clearBackupLogDescription: Permanently delete every backup log row older than {{days}} days. This action cannot be undone.
retention.clearScansDescription: Permanently delete every vulnerability scan (and its findings) older than {{days}} days. This action cannot be undone.

agent.description: Configure how McHarbor communicates with remote agents. These settings affect event collection, heartbeat pings, metrics, and request timeouts for all agent-connected environments.
agent.eventModeDescription: How Docker events are collected from agent environments.
agent.streamWarning: Streaming events monopolizes the agent WebSocket connection, which can block other requests like container inspect and stats. Only use this if you need real-time events and have few containers.
agent.eventPollIntervalDescription: How often to fetch new events from agent environments. Lower values mean more frequent updates but higher load.
agent.pingIntervalDescription: How often to send keepalive pings to connected agents.
agent.metricsEnabledDescription: Enable host metrics collection for agent environments. One-shot stats take ~2s per container through the agent transport.
agent.requestTimeoutDescription: Maximum time to wait for a response from the agent before timing out.

directTransferTest.title: Agent-to-agent transfer test
directTransferTest.description: Verify that one connected agent can reach another agent's direct transfer listener.
directTransferTest.dialogDescription: Direct transfer diagnostics for the selected source and target agents.
directTransferTest.notEnoughAgents: Connect at least two agents to run this test.
directTransferTest.requestFailed: The agent-to-agent transfer test request failed.

interpretation.receiverMissing: The request reached an agent listener that did not have the prepared one-use receiver. This usually means the advertised URL points to the wrong agent, a stale container, or a different process on the same port.
interpretation.bearerMissing: The receiver did not see the bearer authorization header. A proxy or network hop may be stripping Authorization, or the request did not come from the source-agent probe.
interpretation.tokenMismatch: The receiver saw a bearer token, but it did not match the prepared receiver token. This points to stale transfer state, duplicate agent processes, or a token correlation bug.
interpretation.noDiagnostic: The target agent did not report receiver diagnostics. The request may have reached an old or disconnected agent process, or the target agent is not running the diagnostic-capable version.
interpretation.wrongResponder: The HTTP responder marker does not match the prepared target marker. The advertised URL is reaching a different agent listener than the connected target agent.
interpretation.genericFailure: The receiver reported an authorization failure, but the diagnostic flags do not match a known case.

email.selectTypeDescription: Choose the type of email server you want to configure.

exchange.title: Exchange Online Setup Guide
exchange.step1Title: Register an application in Microsoft Entra ID
exchange.step1Description: Go to Azure Portal > Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > New registration.
exchange.step2Description: Add Microsoft Graph > Application permissions > Mail.Send. Grant admin consent.
exchange.step3Description: Go to Certificates & secrets > New client secret. Copy the value immediately.
exchange.step4Description: Copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID from the Overview page.
exchange.step5Description: The from address must be a valid mailbox in your Microsoft 365 tenant.

gmail.title: Gmail Setup Guide
gmail.step1Description: Go to Google Cloud Console > Create a new project or select an existing one.
gmail.step2Description: Go to APIs & Services > Library > Search for Gmail API > Enable.
gmail.step3Description: Go to APIs & Services > Credentials > Create credentials > OAuth client ID. Select 'Web application'.
gmail.step4Description: For service accounts, enable domain-wide delegation and authorize the Gmail send scope.

communications.description: Configure email delivery and notification channels for alerts, events, and system messages.
communications.selectTypeDescription: Choose an email provider or notification platform to configure.
communications.typeSlackDescription: Send notifications to a Slack channel via incoming webhook.
communications.typeDiscordDescription: Send notifications to a Discord channel via webhook.
communications.typeTeamsDescription: Send Adaptive Card notifications to Microsoft Teams.
communications.typeGotifyDescription: Push notifications to a self-hosted Gotify server.
communications.typeNtfyDescription: Send push notifications via ntfy (self-hosted or ntfy.sh).
communications.typeTelegramDescription: Send messages to a Telegram chat via Bot API.
communications.typeSignalDescription: Send messages via a Signal REST API server.
communications.typeWhatsappDescription: Send messages via the WhatsApp Cloud API.
communications.confirmDeleteDescription: This will permanently delete this notification channel configuration.
communications.testDialogDescription: Send a test notification via {{name}} to verify the configuration.

teams.title: Microsoft Teams Setup Guide
teams.step1Description: Go to the channel where you want notifications and click the three-dot menu.
teams.step2Description: Select Workflows > Post to a channel when a webhook request is received.
teams.step3Description: Give it a name and select the channel. The workflow will be created automatically.
teams.step4Description: Copy the webhook URL provided by the workflow and paste it above.

gotify.title: Gotify Setup Guide
gotify.step1Description: Deploy Gotify via Docker: docker run -p 80:80 gotify/server
gotify.step2Description: Open the Gotify web UI, go to Apps, and create a new application.
gotify.step3Description: Copy the token shown for your new application.
gotify.step4Description: Enter your Gotify server URL and app token above.

telegram.title: Telegram Bot Setup Guide
telegram.step1Description: Message @BotFather on Telegram and send /newbot. Follow the prompts to create your bot.
telegram.step2Description: BotFather will give you an API token. Copy it and paste it above.
telegram.step3Description: Add the bot to your group/channel. Send a message, then visit https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates to find the chat ID.
telegram.step4Description: Enter the bot token and chat ID above.

signal.title: Signal REST API Setup Guide
signal.step1Description: Run the Signal REST API server via Docker: docker run -p 8080:8080 bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api
signal.step2Description: Register your Signal phone number with the REST API using the /v1/register endpoint.
signal.step3Description: Verify your phone number using the verification code received via SMS.
signal.step4Description: Enter the server URL, sender number, and recipient numbers above.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp Cloud API Setup Guide
whatsapp.step1Description: Go to developers.facebook.com and create a developer account if you don't have one.
whatsapp.step2Description: Create a new app and select WhatsApp as the product. Set up the WhatsApp Business API.
whatsapp.step3Description: In the WhatsApp dashboard, find your Phone Number ID under the WhatsApp > Getting Started section.
whatsapp.step4Description: Generate a permanent access token in the App Dashboard > WhatsApp > Configuration.
whatsapp.step5Description: Enter the Phone Number ID, access token, and recipient phone number above.

whatsappGateway.title: Self-hosted WhatsApp Gateway Setup Guide
whatsappGateway.step1Description: Set up a self-hosted WhatsApp gateway server (e.g., whatsapp-web.js, Baileys, or similar).
whatsappGateway.step2Description: Ensure your gateway exposes a REST API that accepts POST requests with JSON body.
whatsappGateway.step3Description: Create an authentication token in your gateway's configuration.
whatsappGateway.step4Description: Enter the gateway URL, API token, and recipient phone number above.

whatsappBusiness.title: WhatsApp Business Bot Platform Setup Guide
whatsappBusiness.step1Description: Select a WhatsApp Business API platform provider (e.g., 360dialog, MessageBird, Twilio).
whatsappBusiness.step2Description: Complete the business verification process and set up your WhatsApp Business account.
whatsappBusiness.step3Description: Obtain the API URL, Phone Number ID, and access token from your provider's dashboard.
whatsappBusiness.step4Description: Enter the platform API URL, Phone Number ID, access token, and recipient phone number above.

whatsappSaas.title: Third-party SaaS Setup Guide
whatsappSaas.step1Description: Select a messaging SaaS that supports WhatsApp (e.g., Vonage, Infobip, Gupshup).
whatsappSaas.step2Description: Sign up and configure your WhatsApp messaging channel in the provider's dashboard.
whatsappSaas.step3Description: Obtain the API URL and authentication token from the provider.
whatsappSaas.step4Description: Enter the SaaS API URL, token, and recipient phone number above.

signalBot.title: Signal Bot Setup Guide
signalBot.step1Description: Set up a Signal bot server that exposes a REST API with token authentication.
signalBot.step2Description: Register a phone number or bot identity with the Signal bot server.
signalBot.step3Description: Create an authentication token in the bot server's configuration.
signalBot.step4Description: Enter the bot server URL, API token, and recipient numbers above.

signalD.title: signald Setup Guide
signalD.step1Description: Deploy signald via Docker or from source: docker run -p 15432:15432 signald/signald
signalD.step2Description: Register your Signal phone number with signald using the registration API.
signalD.step3Description: Complete verification with the code received via SMS.
signalD.step4Description: Enter the signald server URL, sender number, and recipient numbers above.

signalSimple.title: Signal Simple Setup Guide
signalSimple.step1Description: Set up a Signal REST API server that does not require authentication.
signalSimple.step2Description: Register and verify your Signal phone number with the server.
signalSimple.step3Description: Enter the server URL, sender number, and recipient numbers above.

storage.description: Configure reusable external storage locations for backups, exports, and future storage workflows.
storage.backupKeyDescription: Generate a 32-byte key for the Docker secret mcharbor_backup_key. McHarbor only shows it once and does not store it.
storage.backupKeyGeneratedWarning: Copy or install this key now. McHarbor does not store generated backup keys, and replacing it later can make existing encrypted backups unreadable unless you keep the old key.
storage.regenerateBackupKeyDescription: This replaces the key currently shown here. Copy or install the current key first; McHarbor cannot show it again. If you install a new key, keep the old key or existing encrypted backups may become unreadable.
storage.backupKeyCopyOnceHint: Copy this key now, then store it as the mcharbor_backup_key Docker secret before running encrypted backups.
storage.selectTypeDescription: Choose the storage provider or protocol you want to configure.
storage.confirmDeleteDescription: This will permanently delete this storage location configuration.
storage.passiveModeDescription: Recommended for FTP/FTPS through NAT, but the server still needs a passive data-port range opened.
storage.ftpSecurityHint: FTP is the original protocol: credentials and files are sent in cleartext. It uses TCP 21 plus dynamic data ports, which is difficult through firewalls and NAT.
storage.ftpsSecurityHint: FTPS is classic FTP protected with SSL/TLS. It encrypts commands and data, but still uses FTP's multi-port active/passive data-channel behavior.
storage.sftpSecurityHint: SFTP is an SSH subsystem. It encrypts all data and authentication natively and uses one firewall-friendly TCP port, normally 22.
storage.ftpPortHint: Default control port is TCP 21. Data transfer may require TCP 20 or passive dynamic ports.
storage.ftpsPortHint: Explicit FTPS commonly uses TCP 21. Implicit FTPS commonly uses TCP 990. Passive data ports may also be required.
storage.sftpPortHint: Default SFTP port is TCP 22 and all traffic stays on this single port.
storage.ftpAuthHint: FTP sends username and password in cleartext unless FTPS is selected.
storage.privateKeyHint: Paste an OpenSSH private key. It is encrypted at rest and is not returned after saving.
storage.passphraseHint: Optional. Required only when the private key is passphrase-protected.
storage.caCertificateHint: Optional PEM CA certificate used to validate the FTPS server certificate.
storage.clientCertificateHint: Optional PEM client certificate for servers requiring mutual TLS.
storage.clientKeyHint: Optional PEM private key for the FTPS client certificate.
storage.secretHint: Leave blank to keep existing secret
storage.credentialsDescription: Credential fields are encrypted at rest and are not shown again after saving.
storage.consentDescription: Save this location, then use Connect to grant account consent. McHarbor stores the returned tokens encrypted.
storage.driveIdConsentHint: Optional. Leave blank to use the default drive returned by the provider.
storage.setupGuideDescription: Use these steps to prepare the provider before saving this storage location.

setupGuide.networkEndpoint: Enter the storage host, port, and reachable network path from the McHarbor container.
setupGuide.tlsEndpoint: Use an FTPS server with a trusted certificate and TLS-enabled listener.
setupGuide.sftpAccess: Create an SFTP user with read and write permissions for the target folder.
setupGuide.networkCredentials: Enter credentials for a dedicated account with the minimum permissions needed.
setupGuide.basePath: Set the base path where McHarbor should store backups and exported files.
setupGuide.sambaShare: Create or choose an SMB share, then enter the share name, domain if needed, and path.
setupGuide.awsBucket: Create an S3 bucket and optional prefix for McHarbor data.
setupGuide.awsCredentials: Create an IAM access key with read and write permissions for that bucket or prefix.
setupGuide.googleProject: Create or choose a Google Cloud project.
setupGuide.googleApi: Enable the Google Drive API for the project.
setupGuide.googleOauthClient: Create an OAuth client ID for a web application and copy its client ID and client secret here.
setupGuide.googleRedirect: Add the redirect URI below to the OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs.
setupGuide.googleConsent: Save the location, then connect Google to grant account consent for the Drive file scope.
setupGuide.microsoftAppPersonal: Create an app registration that supports personal Microsoft accounts.
setupGuide.microsoftAppBusiness: Create an app registration in Microsoft Entra ID for your tenant.
setupGuide.microsoftRedirect: Add the redirect URI below to the app registration.
setupGuide.microsoftTenant: Enter the tenant ID and create a client secret for the app registration.
setupGuide.microsoftGraph: Grant Microsoft Graph file permissions required by this storage location.
setupGuide.sharepointSite: Enter the SharePoint site URL and document library drive ID.
setupGuide.localMount: Mount a host directory into the McHarbor container. The default compose mount maps MCHARBOR_LOCAL_BACKUP_PATH to /mnt/backup.
setupGuide.localPath: Set the local backup path. Use /mnt/backup unless you mounted a different container path.

storage.typeFtpDescription: Store files on a plain FTP server.
storage.typeFtpFtpsDescription: Store files through classic FTP or FTP wrapped in TLS.
storage.typeFtpsDescription: Store files on an FTP server secured with TLS.
storage.typeSftpDescription: Store files over SSH File Transfer Protocol.
storage.typeSambaDescription: Store files on an SMB/CIFS network share.
storage.typeAwsDescription: Store files in an Amazon S3 bucket or S3-compatible endpoint.
storage.typeGoogleDriveDescription: Store files in a Google Drive location.
storage.typeOneDrivePersonalDescription: Store files in a personal OneDrive account.
storage.typeOneDriveBusinessDescription: Store files in a Microsoft 365 business OneDrive account.
storage.typeSharePointDescription: Store files in a SharePoint site document library.
storage.microsoftBusinessConsentDescription: Save this location, then use Connect to grant Microsoft 365 account consent. McHarbor stores the returned tokens encrypted.
storage.tenantIdConsentHint: Required. Use your Microsoft Entra tenant ID or verified tenant domain.
storage.enterBackupKeyDescription: Install an existing base64-encoded 32-byte backup key as the McHarbor Docker secret.
storage.enterBackupKeyHint: Use the original key for existing encrypted backups. Installing a different key can make older backups require their old secret during restore.
storage.installProjectPathHint: Required only when McHarbor runs outside Docker Compose. Leave empty to auto-detect from the container labels. Must be the host directory that contains docker-compose.yml.
storage.localPathHint: McHarbor writes to this path inside the container. Mount it to a host folder with MCHARBOR_LOCAL_BACKUP_PATH so the files live outside the container.
storage.localPathHelper: Default is /mnt/backup. The directory must be writable by the McHarbor container.
storage.typeLocalDescription: Store files on a host-mounted path available to the McHarbor container.

alerts.inAppDescription: Deliver triggered alerts to the bell inbox in the header.
alerts.destinationRequiredHint: Choose at least one destination before saving.
alerts.enabledDescription: Rule is active and can trigger notifications.
